target_customer: Small landlords with single family and small multifamily rentals, starting in Detroit
problem: Landlords paid percentage based fees to traditional property managers; Castle automated tenant finding, rent collection and maintenance dispatch for a flat fee.
business_model: Property management service with flat fee of $79 per unit per month using automation and on-demand labor

founders.name: Max Nussenbaum
education: Venture for America inaugural class fellow, Detroit
founders.background_notes: YC page: product and design focused founder, former graphic designer and web developer.

founders.name: Scott Lowe
previous_startups: Described on the YC page as a 2x YC founder; earlier company not named

exit.reason: The company emailed customers that it was closing; no reason was published in the sources found.

competitors.name: Pillow
competitors.what: Property manager for Airbnb listings, flagged as a possible future competitor in Castle's pitch deck

competitors.name: Cozy
competitors.what: Software for landlords, flagged as a possible future competitor in Castle's pitch deck

technical_complexity.rationale: The software was workflow automation for leasing, payments and maintenance; the YC application cited about 22,000 lines of code. The hard part was operations, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Any property manager could copy a flat fee. Service quality relied on local labor, not proprietary technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (2016-02) says most incumbents charged a percentage of rent; no incumbent bought or copied Castle in the sources found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2016-02) and the company pitch describe incumbent managers charging percentage fees, versus Castle's $79 per unit flat fee. Detroit had many low rent single family units owned by small landlords.

branding.brand_signature: Headquartered in a renovated tax foreclosed mansion in Detroit's Virginia Park, which suited the Castle name
branding.community_and_virality: Local press (Model D, Fox 2 Detroit) covered the founders and the mansion story.

brand_strength.rationale: Local Detroit and TechCrunch coverage existed, but there was no evidence of community or virality and many unrelated Castle property managers exist.

outcome_analysis: Castle raised about $2.75M in its first two years, including a roughly $2M Khosla led seed in April 2016, and managed about 650 units in Detroit, then closed its doors around early 2018 per a customer forum thread. The company did not publish a reason. A third party case study argues the flat fee could not cover acquisition and service costs, so unit economics is recorded as an analyst view only.
notes: The YC directory lists no website for Castle, so there was no company site to fetch. Model D (2016-04) says total raised was $2.75M; CB Insights says $2.12M and the case study says about $3.3M, so totals conflict. The $350K December 2015 round rests on one search summary of a third party case study that I could not open (fetch rate limited). Shutdown date is unclear: a BiggerPockets post says 2/9 with a page date of January 2018, while a Yelp review snippet dated 1/31/2017 mentions closing. Competitors come from a slideshare listing of the pitch deck, which is undated, so source_date 2015 is an approximation. Unit economics is the case study author's opinion, not the company's statement.
